subject: plot externally calculated regression with confidence interval

messages.author: ecf19e9eac4d03c4
messages.subject: plot externally calculated regression with confidence interval
parts:
Hi,

I need help figuring out how to plot in ggplot2 several spline-smoothed regressions that are fit outside of ggplot2.  I have used the "gam" method within stat_smooth (which calls mgcv) for this purpose with good results (see 1st inserted image below), but I need to actually use a monotonically constrained general additive model.


The "scam" package, which builds on the "mgcv" package, fits shape constrained additive models and I've gotten it to produce the ouput I want (see 2nd inserted image below).


This figure has a gam plot on the left and a scam plot (constrained to be monotonically increasing) on the left.  As you can see, the plot on the left has tighter confidence intervals.  The data is the same, and it's also the same gam fit that is plotted in the middle leftmost position in the ggplot2 facet wrapped figure above.

What I would like to do is to recreate the 1st image (i.e. facet wrapped one) with "scam" instead of "gam" regressions, but I don't know how to input into ggplot2 the 95% confidence intervals of regressions calculated externally to ggplot2.

I can figure out how to plot the 95% CIs from the "scam" fits, as it's not much different than plotting externally calculated regression curves (which I've done).  However, it would be ideal to hack/extend stat_smooth to take "scam" as an additional method.  Would this is easy to do?  ...obviously I'd do this on my local ggplot2 installation at first, although an eventual feature addition would be awesome.

Thanks in advance,
Dan.
